rounds.text: Linc Ltd trades at an attractive P/E multiple of 16.9x according to filed statements, presenting a reasonable entry valuation [E1]. This valuation is further supported by a competitive P/E of 17.43x compared to the sector benchmark of 18.08x [E6]. Most importantly, the company demonstrates exceptional capital efficiency with a return on assets (ROA) of 9.77%, which more than doubles the sector benchmark of 4.73% [E8]. Additionally, capital work-in-progress (CWIP) stands at ₹ 34 Cr for March 2026, marking a massive 126.7% increase from the prior year and signaling a strong capex build-up phase for future growth [E33]. The business also rewards shareholders with a steady dividend yield of 1.67% [E4]. Conceded: compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months is -1% and profit growth is -14% [E14, E15].

Linc Ltd is currently exhibiting significant operational deterioration, evidenced by a compounded sales growth of -1% and a sharp -14% decline in profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E14, E15]. This downward trajectory is further confirmed by the signal engine, which explicitly identifies that earnings growth is decelerating [E59]. Investors have reacted to these fundamental headwinds with sustained selling pressure, resulting in a -25% share price decline over the past year and a -22% drop over the last three years [E18, E19]. Consequently, the stock is languishing near the bottom of its 52-week range, sitting only 9% above its low [E5]. While the company is currently in a capital-intensive phase with a 126.7% increase in capital work in progress, this represents a speculative future bet rather than current performance [E33]. Conceded: the company trades at a P/E of 16.9x, which is slightly below the sector benchmark of 18.08x, and maintains an ROA of 9.77% that outperforms the sector median [E1, E6, E8]. Despite these valuation metrics, the persistent negative growth trends and poor long-term price performance suggest that the market remains skeptical of the company's ability to translate its current capital expenditure into meaningful returns [E16, E18, E33].

The bear’s focus on recent growth declines ignores the critical transition signaled by the 126.7% surge in capital work in progress, which indicates that the company is actively investing in future capacity rather than stagnating [E33]. While the bear highlights recent sales and profit contractions [E14, E15], it overlooks the more current evidence showing that sales are actually up on a quarter-over-quarter basis [E55] and that the company is beginning to outperform market expectations as profit growth trends improve relative to price [E50]. Conceded: the company has experienced a -14% decline in profit growth and a -25% share price drop over the past year [E15, E19]. However, the bear fails to acknowledge that the stock is currently undervalued relative to the sector benchmark, trading at a P/E of 16.9x compared to the 18.08x sector average [E1, E6]. Furthermore, the company’s operational efficiency remains superior to its peers, as evidenced by an ROA of 9.77% which is more than double the sector benchmark of 4.73% [E8]. By fixating on historical price performance [E18, E19], the bear misses the fundamental strength of a company that is currently deploying capital to capture future sector growth [E33, E64, E65].

The bull’s reliance on the 126.7% increase in capital work in progress [E33] ignores the reality that this is a speculative expenditure that has yet to translate into actual performance, as evidenced by the current -1% sales growth and -14% profit growth [E14, E15]. While the bull points to quarter-over-quarter sales improvements [E55], these marginal gains are insufficient to offset the broader trend of decelerating earnings growth [E59]. Conceded: the company maintains a higher ROA of 9.77% compared to the sector benchmark of 4.73% [E8]. However, this operational efficiency has failed to prevent a 25% decline in share price over the last year [E19] and a 22% drop over the last three years [E18], suggesting the market is pricing in structural headwinds rather than the bull's projected future capacity. Furthermore, the bull’s claim of undervaluation via P/E [E1, E6] is undermined by the fact that the stock is trading at a premium P/B of 2.16x against a sector benchmark of 1.83x [E7]. Finally, the company’s inability to keep pace with the sector’s 16.3% profit growth and 12.5% sales growth [E64, E65] confirms that the business is currently underperforming its peers despite the ongoing capex build-up [E33].
